column1: # GENERATED AND COMMITTED. Do not edit by hand to make a test pass -- regenerate
# deliberately and review the diff. See README.md in this directory.
#   raw       what a person typed. \uXXXX escapes anything a line-oriented file
#             cannot carry -- and, deliberately, anything INVISIBLE: a literal
#             zero-width space in this file would be indistinguishable from a
#             typo, and the next person to edit it would delete it by accident.
#   expected  the normalised form, or the literal NULL for "rejected"
# Rejection is never repair. A code containing a character outside the alphabet
# is a typo; guessing which character was meant would silently redeem a
# DIFFERENT code and link the wrong account, with no error anybody can see.
# The alphabet is 23456789BCDFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ: no 0/O, no 1/l/I, and no vowels
# at all -- which keeps look-alikes apart and keeps short codes from spelling
# --- the invisibles a copy-paste drags along -------------------------------
# U+00A0 no-break space, U+200B zero-width space, U+FEFF byte-order mark.
# These three produce the "but I typed it correctly" reports.
# Rejected, NOT mapped to their look-alikes.
# Under a Turkish default locale, String.toUpperCase maps 'i' to U+0130.
# Both forms are rejected, and for the same reason: neither is in the alphabet.
# If normalisation ever became locale-sensitive, these two rows would start
# disagreeing with each other on a Turkish server.
# A short or long string still normalises; whether anybody ISSUED it is a
# lookup, not a format question. Conflating them makes a typo report "wrong
# length" when the real answer is "no such code".
# --- case folding must not INVENT an alphabet character --------------------
# Every one of these was a live defect, found by mutating the charset handling
# Unicode case mapping can turn a character that is not in the alphabet into
# one that is. Uppercasing U+017F (long s) gives 'S'; the whole-string fold the
# forum side used also expanded U+00DF to 'SS', U+FB00 to 'FF', and U+FB05 and
# U+FB06 to 'ST'. So typing a sharp s redeemed a code beginning 'SS' that
# belonged to somebody else -- exactly the harm "reject, never repair" exists
# to prevent, committed by the repair step itself.
# The two sides disagreed as well as being wrong: per-character mapping cannot
# expand one character into two, so the game side let only U+017F through. A
# code one connector accepted the other refused.
# Both now map ASCII a-z and nothing else. These rows pin that; the exhaustive
# sweep in LinkCodeFoldingTest and VectorChecks::foldingCannotSynthesise is
# what actually guards it, because eight rows only ever catch eight characters.
# The explicit list cannot enumerate every Unicode space, so both sides fall
# back to a general whitespace test. These rows are what makes that fallback
# observable: drop the /u from the forum side's regex, or swap the game side's
# isWhitespace for a literal set, and only these fail.
